newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital to ban leaded petrol sales from June.
newsitem.headline: China capital to ban leaded petrol sales from June.

text.p: Authorities in Beijing will ban the sale of leaded petrol from June 1 to help improve air quality in the Chinese capital, the China Daily said on Wednesday.

Only sales of unleaded gasoline would be permitted in the city's urban areas from the beginning of next month, but outlying areas would have until January 1, 1998 to implement the ban, the newspaper said.
Petrol stations that sold leaded gasoline after the regulation came into force would be punished, it said but gave no details.
Emissions from Beijing's 1.17 million motor vehicles accounted for about 65 percent of the lead in the capital's air, and the vehicle population had been growing at about 15 percent a year, it said.
The city's biggest gasoline supplier, Yanshan Petrochemical Corp, had spent 1.1 billion yuan ($132.5 million) on equipment renewal and began producing unleaded petrol in March, it said.
China plans to introduce unleaded petrol in all major cities by the year 2000.
